# DKR-020: Containers do not run as root

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

Root in a container is root on the host whenever something else goes wrong: a kernel bug, a mounted socket, a writable host path, an added capability. Docker reads Config.User like this: empty, root and any all zero uid are root, and only the user part of user:group decides. Root fails when the container is also privileged or reachable from outside (a port published on every interface, or a reverse proxy route).

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} user={{.Config.User}}' $(docker ps -aq)
```

## How to fix it

Set USER to a high non root uid in the image (USER 10001), or user: "10001:10001" in compose. Fix file ownership in the image rather than running as root.

## What a fix can break

Images that write to root owned paths or bind ports below 1024 inside the container fail until ownership and ports are adjusted.
